title: Ghostpage prefetch for paged KV + FlashAttn integration (sketch)
content:
Summary:

This note captures a compact sketch for a lightweight predictive prefetch mechanism for our paged KV cache ("ghost pages") and how it should be coordinated with fused FlashAttention kernels. Goal is to reduce tail latency and page-fault stalls for long-context streaming workloads while keeping additional memory and compute overhead small. This is intentionally an exploratory/engineer-sketched doc — experiments will determine which heuristics survive.

Motivation / Problem statement:
- Paged KV gives us strong memory capacity but introduces page-fault stalls when tokens probe unseen KV pages mid-sequence.
- FlashAttention kernels that fuse attention + kv read benefits are sensitive to stalls: a single page miss can force kernel serialization or long device-to-device/dma waits, ballooning tail latency.
- Reactive prefetch (on page miss) is too late for tight SLOs. We need low-cost predictive prefetching that trades some extra bandwidth for reduced 99/99.9p latency.

Idea: "Ghost pages"
- Maintain a tiny per-workload speculative residency prediction structure: ghost pages are compact (bitmap + meta) predictors that indicate likely-to-be-accessed KV pages in the next N tokens.
- Prediction source: simple heuristics + lightweight ML (e.g., per-model logistic regression or tiny LRU/Lambda predictor) trained online from token access traces.
- Use predictions to prefetch pages asynchronously ahead of execution windows used by FlashAttention kernels.

Key design constraints:
1) Low CPU/GPU overhead: predictor should be cheap to evaluate per-request (no full model eval per token).
2) Small memory: ghost metadata must be O(#pages / 64) per active endpoint, not full copies of KV.
3) Minimal false-positive cost: avoid prefetching gigabytes of low-value data. Cap concurrent outstanding prefetches per-request and per-GPU.
4) Integration-friendly: hooks should be implementable without deep rewrites to kernel launch paths.

Architecture sketch:
- Ghost predictor layer (host-side, lightweight): keeps rolling history of accessed pages per request-id and global frequency counters aggregated by model+route. Predictor outputs a ranked list of page_ids to prefetch for the next M tokens.
- Prefetch scheduler (host-side, async): accepts predictions and issues prefetch ops to GPU device memory or peer buffers. Enforces rate limits and prioritization (latency-critical routes higher priority).
- Staging zones: prefetches populate a "hot-zone" (pinned device memory or reserved pool). Kernel read/write paths check residency bitmap and prefer hot-zone first.
- Kernel-level hinting: FlashAttention wrapper receives a small hint buffer per-batch (list of page ids that will be touched). The kernel can speculatively schedule coalesced reads from hot-zone or fall back to on-demand DMA if not resident.

Prediction heuristics (initial experiments):
1) Recency-weighted frequency: keep small counter per-page per-route (8-bit) decayed by time. Predict pages with top-k scores.
2) Windowed stride detection: many token streams show local stride (e.g., reading neighboring pages for contiguous kv segments). Detect and extend.
3) Hot-spot cache: pages that are frequently hit for a route always get high prefetch priority.
4) Tiny learned model: one logistic feature vector [last_page_delta, last_2_delta, freq, recent_hot] per-route trained with SGD online. Output probability threshold.

Rate-limiting and safety:
- Max outstanding prefetches per-request: default 4, configurable.
- Global max prefetch BW / GPU: e.g., 8 GiB/s throttle to avoid saturating PCIe/NVLink during bursts.
- TTL for ghost predictions: predictions older than 50ms are dropped.
- Prefetch dedupe: if page already resident, skip. Keep small dedupe bloom or per-page pending flag.

Integration with FlashAttention kernels:
- Kernel interface: add optional prefetch_hint_buffer arg (device pointer to small list of page ids/residency flags). If provided, kernel can:
  * Pre-warm per-warp pointer tables using hot-zone pointers.
  * Select coalesced load paths optimized for contiguous pages.
  * Avoid heavy branching during inner loops; hints used only to choose fast path vs fallback.
- Fused ops ordering: schedule prefetch earlier than fused attention stage by at least one micro-batch when possible. For streaming, use lookahead tokens to build hints.
- Memory model: prefer device-local pinned allocations for hot-zone to maximize warp-local loads. When prefetch can't place page on same GPU (multi-GPU), fallback to peer-access/copy on demand.

Staging allocator (brief):
- Hot-zone is a ring-allocator backed by a reserved GPU pool. New prefetched pages are appended; eviction happens LRU-like but with protected pages for active inference windows.
- Eviction must respect kernel in-flight references: use epoch counters to ensure kernels referencing a page won't be evicted until completion.

Telemetry and metrics:
- Key metrics to collect: prefetch-hit-rate, prefetch-false-positive-bandwidth, avg/99/99.9 latency delta, page-fault reduced count, extra memory used, prefetch latency (host->device).
- Expose per-route and per-model breakdown to correlate predictor effectiveness.

Testing / microbench plan:
1) Synthetic replay harness: replay long-context traces (from real customers anonymized) with controlled stride patterns and bursts to validate predictors.
2) Kernel microbench: measure single-kernel stall cycles when pages are resident vs missing.
3) End-to-end SLO runs: run stress workload against live runtime with prefetch on/off, varying rate limits and TTLs.

Expected tradeoffs / hypotheses:
- H1: For typical chat-completion traces with locality, a small 2-4 prefetch horizon will cut 99p latency by 30–60% at <10% extra bandwidth.
- H2: Learning-based predictor gives modest improvements over recency heuristics but adds complexity; we should start with heuristics and add online-learned features if needed.
- H3: Kernel hint path must be non-blocking; fallback path should be slightly slower but safe.

Open questions / risks:
- Multi-tenant multi-GPU coherence: how to ensure peer-prefetching doesn't thrash interconnect? Need global allocator throttles per-GPU.
- Correctness: rare race where kernel holds pointer while eviction frees page — need robust epoch mechanism.
- Security: metadata leakage across tenants via predictors — ensure per-tenant isolation.
- Cost: prefetched but unused pages increase bandwidth and heat; need strict throttles and cost observability in Console.

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Implement minimal host-side ghost predictor (recency+freq) and prefetch scheduler prototype (Priya) — target perf harness by 2025-02-20 (MLINF-412).
- [ ] Add kernel hint buffer support to FlashAttn wrapper (Alex) — PR stub and test harness.
- [ ] Add telemetry counters (Diego) and Grafana dashboard mockups.
- [ ] Run synthetic traces (Samira) and produce results for perf review.

Notes to self:
- Keep predictor code path simple and easily toggleable — ops/team will want quick killswitch.
- When experimenting, watch for tail amplification under bursty workloads; throttle aggressively.
- Check existing slabs allocator RFC for eviction epoch idea (slab-prefetch-eviction-hybrid-allocator-rfc).
